story_type: capsule reentry seen from its own hatch camera
hook: A capsule's own camera, hitting the air at 20,000 mph.
narration: This is what a capsule sees when it hits the air at twenty thousand miles an hour.
NASA's new Orion spacecraft flew its first test in December twenty fourteen. No one was aboard.
It climbed thirty six hundred miles above Earth, then started falling back.
At four hundred thousand feet, it met the first thin traces of air.
The air in front of the heat shield is squeezed so hard it glows. Orion's shield reached about four thousand degrees.
That hot, charged gas also cut off its radio. Mission control could only wait.
[short pause] Then two small parachutes opened to steady it, followed by three huge orange and white mains.
They slowed the capsule to twenty miles an hour.
outcome: Orion splashed down in the Pacific about six hundred miles southwest of San Diego.
title: Orion's camera, falling at 20,000 mph
description:
The view from Orion's top hatch camera as the uncrewed capsule fell back through the atmosphere on its first test flight, Exploration Flight Test-1, on Dec. 5, 2014, through the plasma, the parachutes and the splashdown in the Pacific.

Footage: NASA JSC video, via the NASA Image and Video Library: https://images.nasa.gov/details/JSC-Orion-12-5-2014-GA_EFT-1_reentry

facts.claim: View is from Orion's top hatch camera during reentry on EFT-1, Dec. 5, 2014
facts.source_quote: View from Orion's top hatch camera as it reenters the atmosphere during Exploration Flight Test -1 flight on December 5, 2014.
At an altitude of 400,000 feet, the spacecraft encountered the first tendrils of the Earth’s atmosphere

facts.claim: Heating reached about 4,000 degrees F; ionized gas caused a blackout
facts.source_quote: The spacecraft experienced maximum heating of about 4,000 degrees Fahrenheit, proving the worthiness of the heat shield.

facts.claim: Two drogues, then three mains slowing it to 20 mph
facts.source_quote: Next followed deployment of the three main parachutes that slowed the spacecraft to 20 mph.

facts.claim: Splashdown about 600 miles southwest of San Diego; no crew; apogee 3,600 miles
facts.source_quote: Splashdown occurred 4 hours and 24 minutes after launch about 600 miles southwest of San Diego, California.

extra_sources.excerpt: Although EFT-1 didn't include a crew ... raise Orion’s apogee or high point above the Earth to 3,600 miles ... At an altitude of 400,000 feet, the spacecraft encountered the first tendrils of the Earth’s atmosphere ... traveling at 20,000 miles per hour (mph). ... A buildup of ionized gases caused by the reentry heating resulted in a communications blackout ... The spacecraft experienced maximum heating of about 4,000 degrees Fahrenheit, proving the worthiness of the heat shield. ... two drogue parachutes deployed to slow and stabilize the spacecraft ... Next followed deployment of the three main parachutes that slowed the spacecraft to 20 mph. ... Splashdown occurred 4 hours and 24 minutes after launch about 600 miles southwest of San Diego, California.
